2031-08-21	ב׳ אלול תשצ״א	Elul: Rosh Hashana is coming	Elul & Rosh Hashana	In the army we can't get up before dawn for Selichot. When can we say them?	Before Shacharit, before Mincha (after midday), or after midnight. When said by day, it's good for the one leading to wear a tallit.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 581, מדיני הסליחות‎, §4	https://www.yalkut.info/2014/04/21/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%aa%d7%a7%d7%a4%d7%90-%d7%9e%d7%93%d7%99%d7%a0%d7%99-%d7%94%d7%a1%d7%9c%d7%99%d7%97%d7%95%d7%aa/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%AA%D7%A7%D7%A4%D7%90B-B%D7%9E%D7%93%D7%99%D7%A0%D7%99B%D7%94%D7%A1%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%97%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%93	Women	Why do we take challah from dough?	The Torah says: 'The first of your dough, set aside challah as a gift.' So it's a positive mitzva to separate challah from the dough; in Temple times it was given to a kohen. Today, since we're all tamei, the challah is burned instead. 2031-08-22	ג׳ אלול תשצ״א	Elul: Rosh Hashana is coming	Tefilla & shul	The person next to me is saying his Amida a bit out loud. Do I answer Amen?	Yes, the main view is that you answer Amen to the brachot you hear, though you may move away if you can. If you're in Pesukei DeZimra, better move away so you don't hear; but if you did hear a bracha, answer Amen.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 101, תפלה בלב‎, §3	https://www.yalkut.info/2020/07/12/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%a7%d7%90-%d7%a1%d7%a2%d7%99%d7%a3-%d7%91-%d7%aa%d7%a4%d7%9c%d7%94-%d7%91%d7%9c%d7%91/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%A7%D7%90B%D7%A1%D7%A2%D7%99%D7%A3B%D7%91%27B-B%D7%AA%D7%A4%D7%9C%D7%94B%D7%91%D7%9C%D7%91-%D7%92	Brachot	Can I ask for the salt between Hamotzi and my first bite?	Ideally don't speak at all; eat right away. If you spoke about the meal, like asking for salt, you don't repeat the bracha, but other talk means you must say it again. 2031-08-24	ה׳ אלול תשצ״א	Elul: Rosh Hashana is coming	Between people	Our group each puts in the same amount and one name is drawn to win the pot. Is that allowed?	No, it's like gambling and is rabbinically forbidden as theft. A draw where the winner gets a specific item is allowed. No. You may put on the arm tefillin with your watch on: once the seven windings are on your arm, a barrier under the rest of the strap doesn't matter. Someone who takes it off anyway is praiseworthy. 2031-08-25	ו׳ אלול תשצ״א	Elul: Rosh Hashana is coming	Elul & Rosh Hashana	In Selichot, what does 'tochez yadcha bamishpat' mean?	That Hashem's hand hold to 'mishpat', judgment that includes mercy, rather than 'tzedek', strict justice. By the simple meaning, the 'al' (do not) at the start carries on: 'do not let Your hand seize judgment'.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 581, מדיני הסליחות‎, §28	https://www.yalkut.info/2014/04/21/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%aa%d7%a7%d7%a4%d7%90-%d7%9e%d7%93%d7%99%d7%a0%d7%99-%d7%94%d7%a1%d7%9c%d7%99%d7%97%d7%95%d7%aa/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%AA%D7%A7%D7%A4%D7%90B-B%D7%9E%D7%93%D7%99%D7%A0%D7%99B%D7%94%D7%A1%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%97%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%9B%D7%97	Between people	My father doesn't want me learning with a certain chavruta. Must I listen?	Generally no. But if he has real grounds to worry that this friend wastes your time or lowers your fear of Heaven or character, and it pains him greatly, listen. Since it's hard to judge your own case, it's proper to ask a rabbi whether to listen. 2031-08-26	ז׳ אלול תשצ״א	Elul: Rosh Hashana is coming	Elul & Rosh Hashana	In Selichot, what's the difference between 'aniyim' and 'dalim'?	One explanation: an 'ani' is poor, while a 'dal' is so lacking that he's become ill from it. Others say a 'dal' was once rich and lost his wealth, but isn't yet fully poor. Either way, we ask Hashem to act for the sake of both.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 581, מדיני הסליחות‎, §39	https://www.yalkut.info/2014/04/21/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%aa%d7%a7%d7%a4%d7%90-%d7%9e%d7%93%d7%99%d7%a0%d7%99-%d7%94%d7%a1%d7%9c%d7%99%d7%97%d7%95%d7%aa/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%AA%D7%A7%D7%A4%D7%90B-B%D7%9E%D7%93%D7%99%D7%A0%D7%99B%D7%94%D7%A1%D7%9C%D7%99%D7%97%D7%95%D7%AA-%D7%9C%D7%98	Tefilla & shul	I've finished Sim Shalom and said 'Yihyu leratzon'. Can I answer Kaddish and Kedusha?	Yes, but only the first five Amens of Kaddish, 'Yehei shmei rabba' up to 'yitbarach', and 'Kadosh' and 'Baruch' in Kedusha; no Amen to brachot. Before that verse don't interrupt at all, but after the second 'Yihyu leratzon' you may answer everything. If you'll cry during Vidui on Yom Kippur, you can have those tears in mind as you say it. Some say it isn't right to say it with dry eyes otherwise. 2031-08-31	י״ב אלול תשצ״א	Elul: Rosh Hashana is coming	Between people	My parents are very difficult. Must I still honour them?	Yes, even if they're demanding and hard to deal with, especially in old age, and even if everyone takes your side. But if their behaviour is truly unbearable, such as a terrible temper or drunkenness, you may keep your distance, even though you then can't honour them.	Yalkut Yosef, YD 240, את מי חייבים לכבד‎, §1	https://www.yalkut.info/2019/01/31/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%a8%d7%9e-%d7%90%d7%aa-%d7%9e%d7%99-%d7%97%d7%99%d7%99%d7%91%d7%99%d7%9d-%d7%9c%d7%9b%d7%91%d7%93/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%A8%D7%9EB-B%D7%90%D7%AAB%D7%9E%D7%99B%D7%97%D7%99%D7%99%D7%91%D7%99%D7%9DB%D7%9C%D7%9B%D7%91%D7%93-%D7%90	Tefilla & shul	I arrived just as the Kaddish before the Arvit Amida began. Do I wait to answer or start davening?	Start davening, if waiting for the Kaddish means you won't be able to daven Arvit with the congregation and there's no other minyan. Davening with the congregation comes first, even though you'll miss answering "Amen, yehe shemeh rabba". Hurry on by yourself up to 'Ga'al Yisrael', then wait for the congregation and say the Amida with them, so it's still with the minyan. 2031-09-14	כ״ו אלול תשצ״א	Elul: Rosh Hashana is coming	Elul & Rosh Hashana	Why is the shofar kept covered? 2031-11-11	כ״ה חשון תשצ״ב	Year-round	Shabbat	I don't rely on the eruv. Can my children carry my siddur and tallit to shul?	Yes. Where there's a proper eruv, even those who are strict not to carry may give their young children a siddur, chumash and tallit to bring to shul. Where there's no eruv at all, leave them in shul before Shabbat rather than having children carry them.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 301, דיני הוצאה בשבת‎, §4	https://www.yalkut.info/2014/04/09/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%a9%d7%90-%d7%93%d7%99%d7%a0%d7%99-%d7%94%d7%95%d7%a6%d7%90%d7%94-%d7%91%d7%a9%d7%91%d7%aa/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%A9%D7%90B-B%D7%93%D7%99%D7%A0%D7%99B%D7%94%D7%95%D7%A6%D7%90%D7%94B%D7%91%D7%A9%D7%91%D7%AA-%D7%93	Home & kashrut	I'm eating meat and my child is eating cheese at the same table. Is a separator enough?	Better not to rely on it. Some say a separator doesn't work with a child, who might move it and taste the other food, while others allow it; the ruling is to be strict. 2031-11-13	כ״ז חשון תשצ״ב	Year-round	Shabbat	Water boiled before Shabbat cooled down and someone put it on the plata. Can I drink it?	Yes, you may drink it on Shabbat, as long as it had been heated until very hot before Shabbat. But don't do this yourself: according to the Sefardi ruling, putting cooled water back on the plata on Shabbat is forbidden. A woman says 'Modah Ani'. According to the Sefardi minhag, use the regular wording found in all siddurim, pausing slightly after 'bechemla', before 'rabba emunatecha'. 2031-11-14	כ״ח חשון תשצ״ב	Rosh Chodesh Kislev	Erev Shabbat	I made Kiddush at home but ended up eating at the neighbours'. Do I make Kiddush again?	Yes. Kiddush only counts where you eat your meal, so if you eat in another house you must make Kiddush again there. 2031-11-16	א׳ כסלו תשצ״ב	Year-round	Brachot	I said the Ashkenazi ending 'la'asok bedivrei Torah'. Do I repeat?	No. According to the Sefardi minhag the ending is 'al divrei Torah', and Ashkenazim say 'la'asok bedivrei Torah'. Don't change your custom, but if you switched by mistake you needn't repeat.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 47:20	https://www.yalkut.info/2020/07/12/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%9e%d7%96-%d7%9e%d7%94%d7%9c%d7%9b%d7%95%d7%aa-%d7%91%d7%a8%d7%9b%d7%95%d7%aa-%d7%94%d7%aa%d7%95%d7%a8%d7%94/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%9E%D7%96B-B%D7%9E%D7%94%D7%9C%D7%9B%D7%95%D7%AAB%D7%91%D7%A8%D7%9B%D7%95%D7%AAB%D7%94%D7%AA%D7%95%D7%A8%D7%94-%D7%9B	Tefilla & shul	How do I wrap myself in my tallit?	After the bracha, put it over your head with the corners in front. Throw the right side, then the left, back over your left shoulder, pausing briefly each time, then lower it so two tzitzit are in front and two behind. Lowering it onto the body first also has support. 2031-11-21	ו׳ כסלו תשצ״ב	Erev Shabbat	Erev Shabbat	I always light seven candles. Can I cut down to two?	Ideally keep your custom; to drop it for good, it's best to have it annulled (hatara) before three people. For a one-off, like being in hospital with only two candles, no annulment is needed. When you start a custom like this, say it's 'bli neder' so you can change it later.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 263:3	https://www.yalkut.info/2014/04/09/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%a8%d7%a1%d7%92-%d7%94%d7%9c%d7%9b%d7%95%d7%aa-%d7%94%d7%93%d7%9c%d7%a7%d7%aa-%d7%a0%d7%a8%d7%95%d7%aa-%d7%a9%d7%91%d7%aa/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%A8%D7%A1%D7%92B-B%D7%94%D7%9C%D7%9B%D7%95%D7%AAB%D7%94%D7%93%D7%9C%D7%A7%D7%AAB%D7%A0%D7%A8%D7%95%D7%AAB%D7%A9%D7%91%D7%AA-%D7%92	Brachot	Can I answer Amen to Kaddish Titkabal during Pesukei DeZimra?	Yes. Although later authorities disagree, you may answer these Amens, including after 'Titkabal', 'Al Yisrael', 'Yehei shelama' and 'Oseh shalom'. 2031-11-23	ח׳ כסלו תשצ״ב	Year-round	Shabbat	Can I open the extending table for guests on Shabbat?	Yes, you may open a folding table or pull out a table's extension, and fold or close it again afterwards. No. Eating, drinking and idle chatter aren't allowed at the Kotel, a place made holy by Jewish prayer, and don't come just to sightsee or take photos. Even at a brit held there, serve refreshments away from the Kotel area. 2031-11-24	ט׳ כסלו תשצ״ב	Year-round	Shabbat	Can I pull the drawstring on my raincoat hood on Shabbat?	Yes, you may tighten or loosen it, even though it gathers the hood around your head. It isn't considered sewing.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 340, דין תופר ומתיר‎, §4	https://www.yalkut.info/2014/04/12/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%a9%d7%9e-%d7%93%d7%99%d7%9f-%d7%aa%d7%95%d7%a4%d7%a8-%d7%95%d7%9e%d7%aa%d7%99%d7%a8/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%A9%D7%9EB-B%D7%93%D7%99%D7%9FB%D7%AA%D7%95%D7%A4%D7%A8B%D7%95%D7%9E%D7%AA%D7%99%D7%A8-%D7%93	Between people	Can I call my in-laws Abba and Ima?	Yes, some do, and there's nothing wrong with it. But some say not to call your father-in-law "Abba Mari", a title kept for your own parents. 2031-11-25	י׳ כסלו תשצ״ב	Year-round	Brachot	I forgot Baruch She'amar and started Pesukei DeZimra. What now?	If you remember before finishing the Song of the Sea, say Baruch She'amar there, continue, and end with Yishtabach. If you've already finished the Song, don't say Baruch She'amar or Yishtabach. Is it still kosher?	Yes, once they're removed. Long white worms near the spine and fins, or in the belly, are forbidden and must be taken out; shapeless bits under the skin with no head or tail are lenient, but the custom is to remove all of them anyway. No, unless it doesn't look that way: for example you're sheltering from rain or sun, or there's a bench so you seem to be resting. Even then, don't look at the timetable. Which arm do I put tefillin on?	Tefillin go on the weaker arm: most people use the left, but a left-hander who writes and does everything with the left hand puts them on the right. Putting them on the wrong arm doesn't count, even after the fact. 2031-11-28	י״ג כסלו תשצ״ב	Erev Shabbat	Erev Shabbat	Can we eat Friday night dinner on the balcony, where we can't see the candles?	Yes, if it's more pleasant there, for example because of flies inside, since the candles are meant for enjoyment, not discomfort. But make sure you benefit from the candles for at least a short while, or the bracha is wasted.	Yalkut Yosef, OC 263:58	https://www.yalkut.info/2014/04/09/%d7%a1%d7%99%d7%9e%d7%9f-%d7%a8%d7%a1%d7%92-%d7%9e%d7%a7%d7%95%d7%9d-%d7%94%d7%94%d7%93%d7%9c%d7%a7%d7%94/#%D7%A1%D7%99%D7%9E%D7%9FB%D7%A8%D7%A1%D7%92B-B%D7%9E%D7%A7%D7%95%D7%9DB%D7%94%D7%94%D7%93%D7%9C%D7%A7%D7%94-%D7%A0%D7%97	Brachot	Do I say Mezonot on cake for dessert at a bread meal?	Ideally keep cake for after bentching. Cake during the meal gets no bracha, and it's good to have it in mind at Hamotzi. Only a dry, crunchy cake with sweet dough and a nut or honey filling, or a sweet filled wafer, eaten as dessert once you're already full, may get Mezonot. No, you can keep using the same wicks until they're finished; used wicks actually light more easily. Some have the custom to use new wicks each night of Chanukah, in memory of the Beit HaMikdash.
